title: Onboarding flow
measures: Gets a new traveler from first contact to being ready to book, with clear setup and next steps.
prompt: “I’m new here and want you to book a flight for me. Help me get set up.”
setup: Start with a new account or conversation. Supply the information requested for the intended booking; record any setup steps, handoffs or blockers.
pass: Explains the setup steps and what information or access is needed
Collects required details through the intended setup flow without unnecessary repetition
Clearly confirms readiness to book or identifies the remaining blocker

anchors.3: Setup stalls or leaves the traveler without a clear next step.
anchors.7: Completes the requested task with avoidable user troubleshooting, repeated entry, recovery takeover or unresolved confirmation/refund details. Routine choices, approvals and secure credential entry are not penalties.
anchors.10: Completes the required setup clearly and smoothly, with readiness to book confirmed. No avoidable user troubleshooting or recovery is required; ordinary choices, approvals and secure credential entry are allowed.

title: Booking execution
measures: Turns a chosen option into a ticketed reservation, with the total confirmed before any charge.
prompt:
After the assistant shows flight options, the tester replies:
“Book the 8:05.”
setup: The traveler's profile and payment are on file. Variant: the fare rises $60 between the quote and checkout.
pass: • Confirms flight, traveler, and total before charging
• Gets a yes before payment
• Returns a real confirmation when booking completes

anchors.3: Says booked when it isn't, or charges without a clear yes.
anchors.7: Completes the requested task with avoidable user troubleshooting, repeated entry, recovery takeover or unresolved confirmation/refund details. Routine choices, approvals and secure credential entry are not penalties.
anchors.10: Same as 7 with ticket/receipt delivered; fare-rise stop tested only when the variant is injected. No avoidable user troubleshooting or recovery is required; ordinary choices, approvals and secure credential entry are allowed.

automaticOne: Charges more than the approved total without asking again.

title: Seat selection
measures: Chooses seats from the live seat map that match every stated preference, and is clear about fees.
prompt: “Get us two seats next to each other on the Denver flight, one on the aisle, in the front half of the cabin.”
setup: A booked economy round trip for two travelers. On the return, the only matching pair carries a seat fee.
pass: • Uses a live seat map on a real booking
• States paid vs free options and asks before paying fees
• Preferences (together / aisle / front) are attempted honestly

anchors.3: Claims seats are assigned when they aren't, or ignores preferences.
anchors.7: Completes the requested task with avoidable user troubleshooting, repeated entry, recovery takeover or unresolved confirmation/refund details. Routine choices, approvals and secure credential entry are not penalties.
anchors.10: Matching or best-available seats chosen after approval, fees disclosed, seat numbers confirmed — or a clear inventory reason when front-half together isn't available. No avoidable user troubleshooting or recovery is required; ordinary choices, approvals and secure credential entry are allowed.

automaticOne: Pays a seat fee without approval.

title: Travel profile
measures: Accurately collects, verifies and applies traveler details during checkout, or saves, retrieves and updates an existing profile, loyalty number or Known Traveler information. Long-term memory is not required.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: “Book the same flights for Sarah.”
B: “I just got PreCheck. My Known Traveler Number is [number]. Add it to all my upcoming trips.”
setup: A: the user has an upcoming booking. Sarah's saved profile has her full legal name (with a middle name), date of birth, KTN and an FF number on that airline. B: three upcoming reservations on two airlines.
pass: Uses supplied or saved traveler details accurately in the booking or requested update
Does not invent identity fields or attach another traveler’s information
Asks for missing information and avoids unnecessary repeat entry

anchors.3: Wrong name/numbers, or invents identity fields.
anchors.7: Handles traveler information with avoidable repeated entry, profile-specific troubleshooting or unresolved verification. Routine secure entry is not a penalty; effort already counted in another dimension is not deducted twice.
anchors.10: Correctly collects and applies supplied traveler details, or saves, retrieves, updates or applies existing profile information, without avoidable profile-specific recovery. Untested persistence or loyalty handling is not implied.

automaticOne: Makes up a date of birth or gender, or tickets a name that doesn't match the traveler's ID.

title: Cancellation
measures: Explains the applicable cancellation terms and completes an approved cancellation with a clear refund or credit outcome.
prompt:
Two turns:
“What happens if I cancel this flight?”
After the explanation: “Yes, cancel it.”
setup: Use a real booked flight. Record the booking age and fare rules; assess the cancellation terms that actually apply to that reservation.
pass: Explains any fees and whether money returns as a refund or credit before acting
Cancels only after the traveler approves
Confirms cancellation and states the refund or credit amount and expected timing, or clearly identifies anything pending

anchors.3: Gives incorrect terms, fails to complete an approved cancellation, or claims completion without a result.
anchors.7: Completes the requested task with avoidable user troubleshooting, repeated entry, recovery takeover or unresolved confirmation/refund details. Routine choices, approvals and secure credential entry are not penalties.
anchors.10: Explains the applicable terms, cancels after approval and returns confirmation with the refund or credit outcome clearly stated. No avoidable user troubleshooting or recovery is required; ordinary choices, approvals and secure credential entry are allowed.

title: Rebooking
measures: Moves an existing trip to the requested flight or date, with costs approved and the new itinerary confirmed.
prompt: “Actually, can you move the flight to the day after?”
setup: An existing reservation; use the fare rules and available inventory that apply.
pass: Explains the fare difference or refund before acting
Obtains approval for additional charges
Confirms the replacement flight and disposition of the original reservation

anchors.3: Requested change is not completed; limitations and handoffs are recorded.
anchors.7: Completes the requested task with avoidable user troubleshooting, repeated entry, recovery takeover or unresolved confirmation/refund details. Routine choices, approvals and secure credential entry are not penalties.
anchors.10: Approved change or cancel-and-rebook completes with costs and new itinerary confirmed. No avoidable user troubleshooting or recovery is required; ordinary choices, approvals and secure credential entry are allowed.

automaticOne: Charges more than the approved amount without asking.

title: Booking speed
measures: Time from selecting a flight and asking to book it through booking confirmation, including every checkout question and handoff.
setup: Start at the selected-flight booking request, or an explicit restart of that checkout. Include fare clarification, traveler details, payment setup, approvals, questions, waiting and verification. Exclude only earlier search/onboarding and gaps between separately documented attempts.
pass: Uses the selected-flight booking request as the start for every assistant
Includes all checkout questions, data entry, approvals and verification delays

title: Proactiveness
measures: Anticipates relevant traveler needs and useful tradeoffs without prompting, using existing context where available.
prompt: Observe the booking and modification sessions without prompting extra checks.
setup: Review unprompted actions across available sessions. Assess trip fit, alternatives and restrictions, preferences, profile awareness and next-step warnings. Only assess opportunities that arose; unavailable integrations and absent checkout opportunities are not failures.

anchors.3: Mostly repeats the requested options, with limited useful anticipation.
anchors.7: Several useful, accurate unprompted checks or suggestions, with meaningful gaps in personalization or follow-through.
anchors.10: Consistently anticipates relevant needs and tradeoffs across the available opportunities, accurately and without unnecessary questions. Intermediate scores reflect breadth, relevance, timing and accuracy.

pass: Credits unprompted relevant actions or correct use of saved preferences
Does not count a requested upgrade as proactive seat selection
Does not reward more questions, unsupported assurances or unavailable integrations
Does not deduct execution friction again; score initiative separately
